files_changed.summary: A cursor store (ref map) + subscribe() + publishCursor(x,y,page,drawing); cursors never enter state (g1/g3).
One provider owns the single live channel and exposes peers/leader/publish/subscribe (g1).
Subscribes and paints incoming cursors through the peer-cursors leaf, denormalized per page (g2).
Reads the shared presence value instead of opening its own channel.
Export the provider, context hook and layer.
An optional onPointerAt callback forwards the pointer's pixel offset + the Stage size (g3).
An overlay render prop (z2) and a pointer passthrough (g2/g3).
Wraps the view in PresenceProvider, mounts PresenceLayer as the page overlay, and publishes normalized throttled cursors (g3).
Updated the publish signature; added the subscribe/replay/clear test.
2 tests: one channel + value; throws outside.
3 tests: paint denormalized, ignore other page, clear+unsubscribe.

decisions: One PresenceProvider owns the channel: the rail and the layer consume the same value, so a peer's cursor is not fetched twice and only one `live:` channel is open.
Cursors stay out of React state (RULE-20): usePresence keeps a ref map plus a listener set; the layer's subscribe callback runs the painter directly.

The wire carries page-relative 0-1 (RULE-17): the publisher normalizes through geometry with its own size/rotation, and the layer denormalizes with the viewer's, so peers at different zoom/rotation land correctly.
Publishing reuses the ~20 Hz movement-only throttle from 015; publishCursor now takes the page so a cursor is attributed to the page it moved on.
The overlay is a render prop on HighlightedPage rather than a feature import: highlight may not import presence (I3), and the render prop hands the layer the page's displayed size/rotation.
The page-stage callback is a plain function (no Konva, no feature import) so the shared canvas leaf stays presentational.
The provider tracks presence with page 0 (it is view-level); per-page presence tracking is a follow-up, noted.
